metadata.methods_description: EEG data were collected from 27 subjects (age 22.9 ± 3.9 years) with normal hearing and English as primary language. The experiment consisted of two phases: (1) ten one-minute click trials for baseline, and (2) 33 trials each of original and chimeric monophonic music clips presented in shuffled order with 0.5 s inter-trial intervals. Stimuli were presented at 60 dB SPL through ER-2 insert earphones at 48 kHz sampling rate. Participants were seated in a sound-isolating booth approximately 60 cm from a 24-inch monitor. EEG was recorded in BrainVision format. Data collection occurred September-November 2023.

citation_details.title: An updated herpetofaunal species inventory of Iona National Park in southwestern Angola
citation_details.author: Javier Lobón‐Rovira, Pedro Vaz Pinto, François S. Becker, Krystal A. Tolley, John Measey, Bruce Bennet, Bastiaan Boon, Sango de Sá, Werner Conradie
citation_details.abstract: Angola has experienced an incredible increase of the knowledge of its herpetofauna over the past decade. However, accurate biodiversity inventories remain deficient for certain regions of particular conservation interest. We therefore provide an updated checklist of Iona National Park&rsquo;s herpetofauna, with 75 recorded species, including five amphibians and 70 reptiles, 40 of these recorded for the first time in Iona National Park. These species comprise ~80% of the reptile diversity of Namibe Province. Therefore, this work recognises Iona National Park as the most reptile-diverse protected area in Angola and is potentially one of the richest in southern Africa. Consequently, this work enhances the importance of specific conservation plans in the area and the need for further investigation into the hidden biodiversity of this region.
